description:
SHIPPED. Recovery brings up tag 0 and stops. Data-tag materializers are
the distributor's exclusive concern.

FDB's recovery does essentially nothing to storage servers, and ours did
a great deal. Verified in /Users/j5n/Workspace/foundationdb (all four
citations re-checked against the tree at afeef452b):

- The ENTIRE interaction is one key. ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:1692-1698
  sets \xff/lastEpochEnd, commented: "This transaction sets
  \xff/lastEpochEnd, which the shard servers can use to roll back
  speculatively processed semi-committed transactions from the previous
  epoch. It also guarantees the shard servers and tlog servers
  eventually get versions in the new epoch." Storage learns the epoch
  IN-BAND, from the mutation stream.
- RecoveryState::STORAGE_RECOVERED (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:519-520)
  is a STATUS LABEL fired when !newState.oldTLogData.size() -- old tlog
  generations were dropped because storage caught up. Recovery OBSERVES
  storage; it does not drive it.
- Recovery never READS from storage: it rebuilds txnStateStore by
  peeking the old log system (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:1111), then
  reads config/serverTags/localities from there. keyServersPrefix and
  serverKeysPrefix are metadata mutations
  (ApplyMetadataMutation.h:120-121), so routing lives in that
  log-replayed store.
- The recovery version comes from tlogs only, and we already match that
  (log_recovery_planning_phase's calculate_durable_version over
  log_recovery_info). No materializer gates it, so none of the deleted
  work was load-bearing for transaction-system correctness.

DELETED from materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:
- prefer_family_named/3, and with it the PR #198 audit's finding #8
  seam, where recovery's pick and the client-facing pick agreed only by
  construction. The seam is gone, not patched.
- existing_materializers_by_shard/1 (its only consumer was the above)
- ensure_materializers_for_shards/6 and start_materializer_for_shard/5
- extract_shard_tags/1, to_materializer_refs/1,
  create_materializers_for_shards/3 -- the fresh path now calls
  create_and_start_materializer/3 once, for tag 0.

NARROWED: the committed-member read is scoped to
materializers/0/ (materializer_tag_prefix/1) instead of the whole
family. Recovery reads exactly what it uses. Covered by a test that
drives the DEFAULT read path against a stub materializer, so the bounds
under test are the ones production computes.

KEPT, against the original plan: persistence_phase's
build_materializer_keys. The plan said delete it and make the
distributor the sole writer of the materializers/ family. That is wrong
for tag 0 in both directions -- on a fresh cluster nobody else knows
about the materializer recovery just created, and the distributor's own
sweep reads the families through a client transaction that must route to
tag 0 to see anything at all. Chicken-and-egg. Recovery writes tag 0;
the distributor writes everything else. The diff loop stays general
because it is a diff, not a tag-specific rule.

TWO DEFECTS THIS EXPOSED, both fixed here because without them the
change is a silent data bug rather than a refactor:

1. GHOST PRUNING WOULD HAVE DEREGISTERED THE DATA PLANE.
   layout_reference_ids/1 built its reference set from
   shard_materializers, so "recovery did not seat it" meant "ghost" and
   ghosts get deregistered from the coordinator directory. With recovery
   seating only tag 0, that is every data-tag materializer in a healthy
   cluster. It was ALREADY wrong for the non-adopted replicas of a tag.
   Fixed: the reference set now unions in
   materializer_recovery_info_by_id -- the workers that ANSWERED this
   epoch's lock, which is exactly the distinction the doc always claimed
   (a ghost is a registration nothing answered for, on a node that
   cannot deregister itself). Read strictly: a missing key raises rather
   than silently deregistering the cluster.

2. THE DISTRIBUTOR'S VERIFICATION ASKED THE WRONG QUESTION.
   start_verification asked info_fn for [:epoch] and verdicted :current
   on a match. Recovery locks every advertised materializer into its
   epoch and now unlocks only tag 0's -- so a data-tag materializer is
   in the CURRENT epoch and NOT pulling. Verdicted :current, it would
   stay locked for the whole epoch. Locking fences :ingest
   (olivine/server.ex:140) and :apply_transactions (:350) but NOT reads
   ({:get, ...} at :82 and {:get_range, ...} at :109 carry no mode
   guard), so it would go on answering at a frozen version. Silent
   staleness, not a stall -- strictly worse than failing.
   Fixed: a new :mode info fact (the worker is the only process that
   knows whether it is serving), and verification asks [:epoch, :mode]
   and verdicts :current only on epoch match AND mode :running.
   Anything not demonstrably running is adopted; adopting a healthy
   worker costs one lock/unlock and it resumes from its own durable
   version. This bug also existed before this change, for the replicas
   recovery did not pick.

WHY IT IS SAFE: Recruitment.adopt/4 is recruitment minus creation --
locks at the epoch, unlocks at the durable version the worker itself
reports, never removes the worker on failure. That is exactly what
recovery's data-tag path did. The distributor's startup sweep
(server.ex:118) runs after every recovery regardless: read both families
at one pinned version, place the placeholder over the read layout,
publish placeholder refs for uncovered tags in one check-fenced commit,
eagerly recruit the gaps, monitor, and verify every named member.

HONEST COST: between recovery completing and the sweep adopting, data
materializers are not pulling, so reads needing versions past their
durable point wait and time out into a client retry. That window already
existed for every replica recovery did not adopt; this generalizes it
and forces a real answer instead of relying on the pick agreeing.
Routing is not a problem: RoutingData is seeded from the topology
snapshot and then updated IN-BAND from committed materializer_key
mutations (routing_data.ex apply_mutations/2), so the distributor's
publishes reach the proxies without a broadcast.

DIVIDEND: three components with three beliefs about who serves a shard
collapses to two with zero overlap -- recovery owns the transaction
system plus tag 0, the distributor owns the materializers/ family and
elastic membership, the materializer learns in-band
(bedrock-q67.21.6). bedrock-q67.46's locality-aware placement gets
exactly one owner. And the recovery lock set drops from O(shards x
replicas) to O(logs + tag-0 replicas), on the most latency-sensitive
operation in the system.

STILL OPEN, carved out to bedrock-q67.21.20: tag 0 has two membership
owners. The distributor treats it like any other tag and may retire a
member the durable pointer still names, which can stall the next
recovery with a healthy replica sitting right there. Present today; not
introduced here.

GATES: 2759 tests + 13 doctests + 158 properties across seeds 11, 4242,
90210; credo --strict clean; dialyzer 0 errors; formatted.
title: Recovery stops at tag 0: the distributor owns data-tag materializers
